subject: Post-call recap: multi-tenant routing, per-tenant throttles & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finlytics.com>, POC Team <poc@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: multi-tenant routing, per-tenant throttles & pilot next steps

Elena / Finlytics team — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap to make sure we're aligned and to put concrete next steps on the calendar.

Key pain points you shared:
- No reliable per-customer throttles: single global rate limiter causes noisy neighbors and unpredictable latency spikes.
- Route isolation: some customers require dedicated routing/policies by tier (enterprise vs freemium) to meet contractual SLAs.
- Cost leakage during bursts: inability to shape traffic by tenant means heavy overage costs for peak-heavy users.
- Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution and per-tenant latency percentiles are hard to extract from the current stack.

Current stack (as described):
- In-house inference on AWS EKS with a lightweight autoscaler.
- Redis-based prefix cache per tenant for short-lived keys.
- Billing system is third-party; token accounting is batched nightly.

Success criteria you gave (we captured):
1) 99th percentile response time per-tenant < 300ms for standard tier under typical QPS.
2) Ability to apply per-tenant rate limits and soft/hard quotas with predictable failure modes.
3) Route high-value enterprise customers to reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
4) Clear per-tenant cost attribution so you can map spend to customers for billing.

Suggested Redwood approach / options we discussed:
- Pilot: 4-week POC on a small Dedicated pool with 3 tenant profiles (enterprise, standard, free).
- Controls: per-tenant throttles, policy-based routing (pinning to dedicated pools), and quota enforcement with configurable hard/soft limits.
- Observability: token-level traces, 1-min bucketed per-tenant latency and cost breakdowns.
- Fallbacks: automated routing to compatible model variants when reserved capacity is exhausted.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Karthik (me): Send formal POC scope + pricing (attached) and draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) by EOD Friday.
- Elena / Finlytics: Confirm three pilot tenant candidates and regulatory constraints (any data residency or on-prem needs) by Mon 3/8.
- Marcus: Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive to walk your infra team through routing and KV cache integration (proposed week of 3/15).
- Monica: Share SOC2 artifacts and redact-able audit summary if available.

Attachments: redwood-tenant-controls-one-pager.pdf (one-pager), POC_scope.xlsx (scope + deliverables).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag and I'll update. Otherwise I'll follow up with the MAP and a proposed calendar for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: multi-tenant routing, per-tenant throttles & pilot next steps

Karthik — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick confirmations and a couple of clarifications: 

- Confirmed pain points: all accurate. The noisy neighbor issue has caused 2 customer incidents in the last quarter (one resulted in a credit).
- Current stack notes: we do nightly token accounting today which makes near-real-time cost attribution impossible; moving that to per-minute would help the billing team.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II is in progress (expected June), but we do have PCI scope limits for one enterprise customer which may need VPC options.

We're comfortable moving forward with a pilot. Proposed timeline: kickoff week of 3/15, 4-week run. My team will identify 3 tenants for the pilot by Monday 3/8.

Couple of asks before the technical deep-dive: 
1) Can you share an example token-distribution profile (p95/p99) for a multi-tenant workload?
2) How does Redwood expose per-tenant quotas in the API (error codes, backoff recommendations)?

I'll upload the tenant list and any redacted contract language to the shared folder once we confirm candidates.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Product
